main_issue: Where to hold the farewell lunch: keep the Korean barbecue (beef cooked at tables) or switch to somewhere D and C can manage, such as a zi char place.

A-B.evidence: B pushed to keep the BBQ (8, 14) and A resisted (13, 15); B conceded (16) and then agreed to zi char (20).

A-C.evidence: C raised a time limit (5) and suggested a food court (17); A asked if zi char is quick enough (21, 24) and offered to pre-order (26); C said 'I think so' (25), tentatively accepting.

A-D.evidence: A dropped the BBQ once D explained the religious reason (13), and A backed D's zi char idea (19, 24).

B-C.evidence: B and C never addressed each other; B accepted zi char (20), C tentatively accepted a quick zi char place (25).

B-D.evidence: B wanted to keep the BBQ or find tables without the grill (14), against D's need; B conceded (16) and endorsed D's zi char suggestion (20).

C-D.evidence: C suggested a food court (17), D countered with zi char (18); D proposed a fast place near the MRT (23), and C said 'I think so' (25).
